key_insight: Quantum impurity solvers could enable screening of strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials by improving predictions of vacancy energetics and electronic conductivity.
engineering_relevance: A continuum electrode model links microscopic material properties to SOFC and SOEC performance while accounting for oxygen exchange, transport, microstructure, and electrode thickness.
method: Use DFT screening to shortlist materials and construct atomistic electrode/electrolyte interface models.
Apply GW+DMFT or SEET embedding, with quantum solvers supplying finite-temperature impurity Green’s functions.
Map predicted interface observables to engineering metrics and estimate potential business value under deployment scenarios.
evidence_signal: The abstract provides illustrative logical-qubit counts and proposes benchmarks for converged vacancy and migration energetics against the best applicable classical solvers, rather than reporting demonstrated quantum advantage.
watch_item: Practical advantage remains contingent on thermal-state preparation, simulation, measurement, and repeated-solve costs.
paper_title: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation
